sentences.text: This Criminal Original Petition has been filed seeking to quash the First Information Report in Crime No.28 of 2021 on the file of the 1st respondent, filed for the offence under Sections 406 and 420 IPC.

2.It is alleged in the FIR that the petitioner was a Director in a company by name RSL Property Development Limited; that the defacto complainant / 2nd respondent approached the petitioner for purchase of the property belonging to the said company; that the defacto complainant agreed to purchase the said property for a total sale consideration of Rs. 97,89,000/-; that when the defacto complainant went for registration of the said property, he found that the property was subject to attachment by the ESI Corporation; that therefore, the defacto complainant had to pay an additional sum of Rs.51,54,759/- to clear the dues to ESI Corporation; that the petitioner had suppressed the fact that the property was subject to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis attachment by ESI Corporation and caused wrongful loss to the tune of Rs.51,54,759/- to the defacto complainant; that when the defacto complainant made demand for the said sum the petitioner threatened and abused him in filthy language.
Hence, the complaint.
3.Mr.Ajmal Khan, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner would submit that the allegation in the First Information Report even if accepted to be true would not attract the offences alleged.
Admittedly, 2nd respondent had paid the dues to ESI Corporation on 30.01.2013.
The 2 nd respondent was aware of the attachment before the ESI Corporation as the encumbrance certificate disclosed the attachment.
The 2nd respondent ought have filed suit for recovery of money from the petitioner, even if the allegation is accepted to be true within three years from 30.01.2013.
The present complaint is nothing but an abuse of process of law to get over the law of limitation for recovery of money before the Civil Court.
The impugned FIR which is filed in the year 2021, eight years after the money allegedly became due is nothing but an abuse of process of law.

The learned Senior Counsel further submitted that in any event, the offence under Section 406 IPC is not made,
since there is no entrustment of property.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 4.The
learned counsel for the 2nd respondent submitted that the 2nd respondent was deceived by the petitioner and was made to pay Rs.51,54,799/-.
He had been making request to the petitioner to repay the said amount paid by him to the ESI Corporation.
However, the petitioner had been delaying the payment and now he would state that he is not liable to pay the said money.
This act establishes that the petitioner made false representation and hence liable for the offences and that there is no delay in lodging the FIR.

5.The learned Government Advocate (Criminal Side) submitted that the allegations in the FIR has to be investigated and the FIR cannot be scuttled at a nascent stage and prayed for dismissal of the quash petition.

6.This Court finds that admittedly the petitioner and the 2 nd respondent had entered into a sale S.Ramasamy vs The State Rep. By on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107084340/

sentences.text: The sale transaction was concluded in the year 2012.
The 2nd respondent is said to have paid Rs.51,54,799/- to the ESI Corporation, which had allegedly attached the property belonging to the petitioner's company.
This Court finds that https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis thereafter, the 2nd respondent has not taken any steps for recovery of the said money.
The limitation prescribed to recover the money is three years.
The 2nd respondent has come up with the impugned complaint after eight years, alleging the offence of cheating.
This Court finds that the impugned FIR is clearly an abuse of process of law to get over the law of limitation for recovery of money.
7.A civil dispute relating to a money transaction is sought to be projected as a case of cheating after eight years.
Even otherwise, the conduct of the parties during and after the sale transaction as alleged in the FIR do not suggest that the 2nd respondent made the payment due to any alleged deception.
The 2nd respondent was aware of the consequences of his making the payment.
Strangely he had not approached the civil Court by filing a suit for recovery of money.
The offence under Section 420 IPC is not made out.
Hence the continuation of the investigation on an FIR which does not disclose a cognizable offence would be an abuse of process of law.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
8.The offence under Section 406 IPC is also not made out as there is no allegation of entrustment of any property.
The said provision has been mechanically added in the impugned FIR without appreciating the ingredients of the offence of criminal breach of trust.
9.For the above reasons, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed and the First Information Report in Crime No.28 of 2021 on the file of the 1st respondent is quashed.
Connected, Criminal Miscellaneous Petition is closed.
